questions.prompt: Keating states that all forms of electromagnetic radiation, including visible light, travel at roughly:
choices: A The speed of sound in air.
B 300,000 km/s (about 186,000 miles per second), the fastest speed anything can travel.
C Variable speeds depending on wavelength only.
D Zero in vacuum.
questions.explain: He gives ~300,000 km/s as the universal speed of EM radiation / light.

questions.prompt: Compared with a reflecting telescope, how does Keating describe the simplest refracting telescope?
choices: A It uses only mirrors and no lenses.
B It is very similar to the human eye and uses (convex) lenses to focus light.
C It was invented solely by Newton.
D It cannot form images at all.
questions.explain: He likens the simplest refractor to the eye and discusses convex lenses.

questions.prompt: Who created the reflecting telescope that Keating highlights?
choices: A Galileo.
B Isaac Newton.
C Vermeer.
D Doppler.
questions.explain: He attributes the reflecting telescope to Isaac Newton's experiments.

questions.prompt: About how large does Keating say the biggest astronomical lenses ever made are, and how do space telescopes compare?
choices: A About 1 m diameter lenses; some space telescopes are about six times bigger.
B Lenses of 100 m; space telescopes are smaller.
C No lens larger than a contact lens was ever made.
D Only mirrors under 10 cm exist.
questions.explain: He cites ~1 m as the largest astronomical lens and larger space telescopes.

questions.prompt: Christian Doppler, in Keating's account, showed that a moving object causes:
choices: A Gravity to reverse.
B A change (shift) in the wavelength of waves from that object.
C Telescopes to stop working.
D Stars to become black holes instantly.
questions.explain: Doppler's result is that motion shifts wavelength—foundation of redshift/blueshift.
